### Write functions to determine differences

First, evaluate_group_sizes() is a diagnostic to determine if difference tests can be run. 

Similarly, summarize_group_sizes() will output the number of observations for each group.

The differences() function will:
- Filter out groups with <2 observations
- Use shapiro.test() on ANOVA residuals to test the normality of the distribution, and output to "Distribution" whether the residual distribution is normal (P>0.05), has minor non-normality (W>0.9 but P<0.05), or has major non-normality (W<0.9, P<0.01)
- Use bartlett.test() if residuals are normally distributed or leveneTest() if not to test for homogeneity of variance in the data, and output to "Variance" whether the variance is homogeneous (P>0.05) or heterogeneous (P<0.05)
- If data meet parametric assumptions (normal distribution or minor non-normality, and homogeneity of variance), then procede with one-way ANOVA and Tukey's HSD post hoc test, or otherwise (major non-normality and/or heterogeneity of variance), use Kruskal-Wallis and Dunn's Test
- Output tests used, P-values for the post hoc tests, and significance level indicators for a quick look
- Tell which factor group has a higher mean (if parametric) or median (non-parametric) value for the continuous variable in a Comparison column

The differences_multifactor() function will accept a vector of factors (1-3) and runs the same tests as differences() with these differences: 
- Uses a model formula to assess all factors and interactions
- Uses two-way or three-way ANOVA for parametric data, and Aligned Ranks Transformation (ART) ANOVA for non-parametric

Uses car, lme4, emmeans, and ARTool packages.


```{r set up group size functions}

#pairwise comparisons

#first look at group sizes
evaluate_group_sizes <- function(data, factors, continuous_vars) {
  insufficient_groups <- list()

  for (cont_var in continuous_vars) {
    for (factor in factors) {
      filtered_data <- na.omit(data[, c(factor, cont_var)]) #remove NA values for continuous variable and factor

      #drop unused factor levels
      if (is.factor(filtered_data[[factor]])) {
        filtered_data[[factor]] <- droplevels(filtered_data[[factor]])
      }

      group_sizes <- table(filtered_data[[factor]]) #calculate group sizes
      
      #identify groups with fewer than 2 observations
      insufficient <- group_sizes[group_sizes < 2]
      if (length(insufficient) > 0) {
        insufficient_groups[[paste(cont_var, factor, sep = "_")]] <- data.frame(
          Factor = factor,
          Continuous_Var = cont_var,
          Group = names(insufficient),
          Observations = as.numeric(insufficient)
        )
      }
    }
  }

  #combine results into a single dataframe
  if (length(insufficient_groups) > 0) {
    return(bind_rows(insufficient_groups, .id = "Combination"))
  } else {
    return(data.frame(
      Combination = character(),
      Factor = character(),
      Continuous_Var = character(),
      Group = character(),
      Observations = numeric()
    ))
  }
}

summarize_group_sizes <- function(data, factors, continuous_vars) {
  group_summary <- list()
  
  for (cont_var in continuous_vars) {
    for (factor in factors) {
      filtered_data <- na.omit(data[, c(factor, cont_var)])
      
      group_sizes <- table(filtered_data[[factor]])
      
      group_summary[[paste(cont_var, factor, sep = "_")]] <- data.frame(
        Continuous_Var = cont_var,
        Factor = factor,
        Group = names(group_sizes),
        Observations = as.numeric(group_sizes)
      )
    }
  }
  
  return(bind_rows(group_summary))
}

#analysis function with Shapiro test, Levene test, Bartlett's test, group size evaluation, and NA omission
differences <- function(data, factors, continuous_vars) {
  results_list <- list()

  for (cont_var in continuous_vars) {
    for (factor in factors) {
      #remove NA values for the current continuous variable and factor
      filtered_data <- na.omit(data[, c(factor, cont_var)])

      #check if all groups for the factor have at least 2 observations
      group_sizes <- table(filtered_data[[factor]])
      if (any(group_sizes < 2)) {
        #if a group has fewer than 2 observations, skip analysis and add a note
        results_list[[paste(cont_var, factor, sep = "_")]] <- data.frame(
          Comparison = NA,
          Factor = factor,
          Continuous_Var = cont_var,
          Distribution = "Skipped",
          Variance = "Skipped",
          Test = "Skipped (Insufficient group size)",
          P_Value = NA,
          Significance = "Not significant"
        )
        next
      }

      #step 1: test normality using Shapiro-Wilk test on residuals
      anova_res <- aov(as.formula(paste(cont_var, "~", factor)), data = filtered_data)
      residuals <- residuals(anova_res)
      shapiro <- shapiro.test(residuals)
      
      #determine normality category
      if (shapiro$p.value > 0.05) {
        distribution_status <- "Normal"
      } else if (shapiro$statistic > 0.9) {
        distribution_status <- "Minor non-normality"
      } else {
        distribution_status <- "Major non-normality"
      }

      #step 2: test homogeneity of variances
      #use Bartlett's test if normally distributed, Levene's test if not
      if (distribution_status == "Normal") {
        bartlett <- bartlett.test(as.formula(paste(cont_var, "~", factor)), data = filtered_data)
        variance_test_pvalue <- bartlett$p.value
        variance_test_name <- "Bartlett"
      } else {
        levene <- car::leveneTest(as.formula(paste(cont_var, "~", factor)), data = filtered_data)
        variance_test_pvalue <- levene$`Pr(>F)`[1]
        variance_test_name <- "Levene"
      }
      
      #determine homogeneity status
      variance_status <- ifelse(variance_test_pvalue > 0.05, "Homogeneous", "Heterogeneous")

      #step 3: decide which statistical test to use based on parametric assumptions
      #parametric assumptions met: normal distribution (or minor non-normality) AND homogeneous variances
      use_parametric <- (distribution_status %in% c("Normal", "Minor non-normality")) && (variance_status == "Homogeneous")

      if (use_parametric) {
        #ANOVA and Tukey's HSD
        tukey <- TukeyHSD(anova_res)

        #extract pairwise comparisons and P-values
        if (!is.null(tukey[[1]])) {
          #calculate group means for ordering comparisons
          group_means <- tapply(filtered_data[[cont_var]], filtered_data[[factor]], mean, na.rm = TRUE)
          
          comparisons <- rownames(tukey[[1]])
          p_values <- tukey[[1]][, "p adj"]
          
          #reorder comparisons so higher mean is listed first
          reordered_comparisons <- sapply(comparisons, function(comp) {
            groups <- strsplit(comp, "-")[[1]]
            group1 <- trimws(groups[1])
            group2 <- trimws(groups[2])
            
            if (group_means[group1] > group_means[group2]) {
              paste(group1, ">", group2)
            } else {
              paste(group2, ">", group1)
            }
          })
          
          sig_pairs <- data.frame(
            Comparison = reordered_comparisons,
            Factor = factor,
            Continuous_Var = cont_var,
            Distribution = distribution_status,
            Variance = variance_status,
            Test = "Tukey's HSD (ANOVA)",
            P_Value = p_values,
            Significance = case_when(
              p_values <= 0.001 ~ "***",
              p_values <= 0.01 ~ "**",
              p_values <= 0.05 ~ "*",
              TRUE ~ "Not significant"
            )
          )

          results_list[[paste(cont_var, factor, sep = "_")]] <- sig_pairs
        } else {
          #if no valid groupings are present, return an empty dataframe
          results_list[[paste(cont_var, factor, sep = "_")]] <- data.frame(
            Comparison = NA,
            Factor = factor,
            Continuous_Var = cont_var,
            Distribution = distribution_status,
            Variance = variance_status,
            Test = "Tukey's HSD (No significant groupings)",
            P_Value = NA,
            Significance = "Not significant"
          )
        }
      } else {
        #Kruskal-Wallis and Dunn's Test for non-parametric data
        kruskal <- kruskal.test(as.formula(paste(cont_var, "~", factor)), data = filtered_data)

        if (kruskal$p.value < 0.05) { #Dunn's Test if Kruskal-Wallis is significant
          dunn <- dunn.test(filtered_data[[cont_var]], filtered_data[[factor]], method = "bonferroni", kw = FALSE)

          #calculate group medians for ordering comparisons
          group_medians <- tapply(filtered_data[[cont_var]], filtered_data[[factor]], median, na.rm = TRUE)
          
          comparisons <- dunn$comparisons
          p_values <- dunn$P.adjusted
          
          #reorder comparisons so higher median is listed first
          reordered_comparisons <- sapply(comparisons, function(comp) {
            groups <- strsplit(comp, " - ")[[1]]
            group1 <- trimws(groups[1])
            group2 <- trimws(groups[2])
            
            if (group_medians[group1] > group_medians[group2]) {
              paste(group1, ">", group2)
            } else {
              paste(group2, ">", group1)
            }
          })
          
          sig_pairs <- data.frame(
            Comparison = reordered_comparisons,
            Factor = factor,
            Continuous_Var = cont_var,
            Distribution = distribution_status,
            Variance = variance_status,
            Test = "Dunn's Test (Kruskal-Wallis)",
            P_Value = p_values,
            Significance = case_when(
              p_values <= 0.001 ~ "***",
              p_values <= 0.01 ~ "**",
              p_values <= 0.05 ~ "*",
              TRUE ~ "Not significant"
            )
          ) %>%
            filter(P_Value < 1)

          results_list[[paste(cont_var, factor, sep = "_")]] <- sig_pairs
        } else {
          results_list[[paste(cont_var, factor, sep = "_")]] <- data.frame(
            Comparison = NA,
            Factor = factor,
            Continuous_Var = cont_var,
            Distribution = distribution_status,
            Variance = variance_status,
            Test = "Kruskal-Wallis (NS)",
            P_Value = NA,
            Significance = "Not significant"
          )
        }
      }
    }
  }

  #combine results for all factors and continuous variables
  results_df <- bind_rows(results_list, .id = "Analysis_Combination")
  
  return(results_df)
}

#analysis function for multifactor models with Shapiro test, Levene test, Bartlett's test, group size evaluation, and NA omission
differences_multifactor <- function(data, factors, continuous_vars) {
  results_list <- list()

  for (cont_var in continuous_vars) {
    # Create formula with all factors
    factor_formula <- paste(factors, collapse = " * ")
    full_formula <- as.formula(paste(cont_var, "~", factor_formula))
    
    # Remove NA values for the current continuous variable and all factors
    cols_needed <- c(factors, cont_var)
    filtered_data <- na.omit(data[, cols_needed])

    # Check if all groups for each factor have at least 2 observations
    insufficient_groups <- FALSE
    for (factor in factors) {
      group_sizes <- table(filtered_data[[factor]])
      if (any(group_sizes < 2)) {
        insufficient_groups <- TRUE
        break
      }
    }
    
    if (insufficient_groups) {
      # If any factor has groups with fewer than 2 observations, skip analysis and add a note
      results_list[[cont_var]] <- data.frame(
        Comparison = NA,
        Factors = paste(factors, collapse = " * "),
        Continuous_Var = cont_var,
        Distribution = "Skipped",
        Variance = "Skipped",
        Test = "Skipped (Insufficient group size)",
        P_Value = NA,
        Significance = "Not significant"
      )
      next
    }

    # Step 1: Test normality using Shapiro-Wilk test on residuals
    anova_res <- aov(full_formula, data = filtered_data)
    residuals <- residuals(anova_res)
    shapiro <- shapiro.test(residuals)
    
    # Determine normality category
    if (shapiro$p.value > 0.05) {
      distribution_status <- "Normal"
    } else if (shapiro$statistic > 0.9) {
      distribution_status <- "Minor non-normality"
    } else {
      distribution_status <- "Major non-normality"
    }

    # Step 2: Test homogeneity of variances
    # Create interaction groups for both Bartlett and Levene tests
    if (length(factors) == 1) {
      interaction_groups <- filtered_data[[factors[1]]]
    } else if (length(factors) == 2) {
      interaction_groups <- interaction(filtered_data[[factors[1]]], filtered_data[[factors[2]]])
    } else if (length(factors) == 3) {
      interaction_groups <- interaction(filtered_data[[factors[1]]], filtered_data[[factors[2]]], filtered_data[[factors[3]]])
    }
    
    # Use Bartlett's test if normally distributed, Levene's test if not
    if (distribution_status == "Normal") {
      bartlett <- bartlett.test(filtered_data[[cont_var]], interaction_groups)
      variance_test_pvalue <- bartlett$p.value
    } else {
      levene <- car::leveneTest(filtered_data[[cont_var]], interaction_groups)
      variance_test_pvalue <- levene$`Pr(>F)`[1]
    }

    # Step 3: Decide which statistical test to use
    # Parametric assumptions met: Normal distribution (or minor non-normality) AND homogeneous variances
    use_parametric <- (distribution_status %in% c("Normal", "Minor non-normality")) && (variance_status == "Homogeneous")

    if (use_parametric) {
      # ANOVA and Tukey's HSD
      tukey <- TukeyHSD(anova_res)

      # Extract pairwise comparisons and P-values for each factor
      for (i in seq_along(tukey)) {
        factor_name <- names(tukey)[i]
        
        if (!is.null(tukey[[i]])) {
          # Calculate group means for ordering comparisons
          group_means <- tapply(filtered_data[[cont_var]], filtered_data[[factor_name]], mean, na.rm = TRUE)
          
          comparisons <- rownames(tukey[[i]])
          p_values <- tukey[[i]][, "p adj"]
          
          # Reorder comparisons so higher mean is listed first
          reordered_comparisons <- sapply(comparisons, function(comp) {
            groups <- strsplit(comp, "-")[[1]]
            group1 <- trimws(groups[1])
            group2 <- trimws(groups[2])
            
            if (group_means[group1] > group_means[group2]) {
              paste(group1, ">", group2)
            } else {
              paste(group2, ">", group1)
            }
          })
          
          sig_pairs <- data.frame(
            Comparison = reordered_comparisons,
            Factors = paste(factors, collapse = " * "),
            Continuous_Var = cont_var,
            Distribution = distribution_status,
            Variance = variance_status,
            Test = paste("Tukey's HSD (ANOVA) -", factor_name),
            P_Value = p_values,
            Significance = case_when(
              p_values <= 0.001 ~ "***",
              p_values <= 0.01 ~ "**",
              p_values <= 0.05 ~ "*",
              TRUE ~ "Not significant"
            )
          )

          results_list[[paste(cont_var, factor_name, sep = "_")]] <- sig_pairs
        }
      }
    } else {
      # Kruskal-Wallis and Dunn's Test for each factor
      for (factor in factors) {
        kruskal <- kruskal.test(as.formula(paste(cont_var, "~", factor)), data = filtered_data)

        if (kruskal$p.value < 0.05) { # Dunn's Test if Kruskal-Wallis is significant
          dunn <- dunn.test(filtered_data[[cont_var]], filtered_data[[factor]], method = "bonferroni", kw = FALSE)

          # Calculate group medians for ordering comparisons
          group_medians <- tapply(filtered_data[[cont_var]], filtered_data[[factor]], median, na.rm = TRUE)
          
          comparisons <- dunn$comparisons
          p_values <- dunn$P.adjusted
          
          # Reorder comparisons so higher median is listed first
          reordered_comparisons <- sapply(comparisons, function(comp) {
            groups <- strsplit(comp, " - ")[[1]]
            group1 <- trimws(groups[1])
            group2 <- trimws(groups[2])
            
            if (group_medians[group1] > group_medians[group2]) {
              paste(group1, ">", group2)
            } else {
              paste(group2, ">", group1)
            }
          })
          
          sig_pairs <- data.frame(
            Comparison = reordered_comparisons,
            Factors = paste(factors, collapse = " * "),
            Continuous_Var = cont_var,
            Distribution = distribution_status,
            Variance = variance_status,
            Test = paste("Dunn's Test (Kruskal-Wallis) -", factor),
            P_Value = p_values,
            Significance = case_when(
              p_values <= 0.001 ~ "***",
              p_values <= 0.01 ~ "**",
              p_values <= 0.05 ~ "*",
              TRUE ~ "Not significant"
            )
          ) %>%
            filter(P_Value < 1)

          results_list[[paste(cont_var, factor, sep = "_")]] <- sig_pairs
        } else {
          results_list[[paste(cont_var, factor, sep = "_")]] <- data.frame(
            Comparison = NA,
            Factors = paste(factors, collapse = " * "),
            Continuous_Var = cont_var,
            Distribution = distribution_status,
            Variance = variance_status,
            Test = paste("Kruskal-Wallis (NS) -", factor),
            P_Value = NA,
            Significance = "Not significant"
          )
        }
      }
    }
  }

  # Combine results for all factors and continuous variables
  results_df <- bind_rows(results_list, .id = "Analysis_Combination")
  
  return(results_df)
}
```

```{r set up one-way pairwise comparison function}

#pairwise comparisons

#analysis function with Shapiro test, Levene test, Bartlett's test, group size evaluation, and NA omission
differences <- function(data, factors, continuous_vars) {
  results_list <- list()

  for (cont_var in continuous_vars) {
    for (factor in factors) {
      #remove NA values for the current continuous variable and factor
      filtered_data <- na.omit(data[, c(factor, cont_var)])

      #check if all groups for the factor have at least 2 observations
      group_sizes <- table(filtered_data[[factor]])
      if (any(group_sizes < 2)) {
        #if a group has fewer than 2 observations, skip analysis and add a note
        results_list[[paste(cont_var, factor, sep = "_")]] <- data.frame(
          Comparison = NA,
          Factor = factor,
          Continuous_Var = cont_var,
          Distribution = "Skipped",
          Variance = "Skipped",
          Test = "Skipped (Insufficient group size)",
          P_Value = NA,
          Significance = "Not significant"
        )
        next
      }

      #step 1: test normality using Shapiro-Wilk test on residuals
      anova_res <- aov(as.formula(paste(cont_var, "~", factor)), data = filtered_data)
      residuals <- residuals(anova_res)
      shapiro <- shapiro.test(residuals)
      
      #determine normality category
      if (shapiro$p.value > 0.05) {
        distribution_status <- "Normal"
      } else if (shapiro$statistic > 0.9) {
        distribution_status <- "Minor non-normality"
      } else {
        distribution_status <- "Major non-normality"
      }

      #step 2: test homogeneity of variances
      #use Bartlett's test if normally distributed, Levene's test if not
      if (distribution_status == "Normal") {
        bartlett <- bartlett.test(as.formula(paste(cont_var, "~", factor)), data = filtered_data)
        variance_test_pvalue <- bartlett$p.value
        variance_test_name <- "Bartlett"
      } else {
        levene <- car::leveneTest(as.formula(paste(cont_var, "~", factor)), data = filtered_data)
        variance_test_pvalue <- levene$`Pr(>F)`[1]
        variance_test_name <- "Levene"
      }
      
      #determine homogeneity status
      variance_status <- ifelse(variance_test_pvalue > 0.05, "Homogeneous", "Heterogeneous")

      #step 3: decide which statistical test to use based on parametric assumptions
      #parametric assumptions met: normal distribution (or minor non-normality) AND homogeneous variances
      use_parametric <- (distribution_status %in% c("Normal", "Minor non-normality")) && (variance_status == "Homogeneous")

      if (use_parametric) {
        #ANOVA and Tukey's HSD
        tukey <- TukeyHSD(anova_res)

        #extract pairwise comparisons and P-values
        if (!is.null(tukey[[1]])) {
          #calculate group means for ordering comparisons
          group_means <- tapply(filtered_data[[cont_var]], filtered_data[[factor]], mean, na.rm = TRUE)
          
          comparisons <- rownames(tukey[[1]])
          p_values <- tukey[[1]][, "p adj"]
          
          #reorder comparisons so higher mean is listed first
          reordered_comparisons <- sapply(comparisons, function(comp) {
            groups <- strsplit(comp, "-")[[1]]
            group1 <- trimws(groups[1])
            group2 <- trimws(groups[2])
            
            if (group_means[group1] > group_means[group2]) {
              paste(group1, ">", group2)
            } else {
              paste(group2, ">", group1)
            }
          })
          
          sig_pairs <- data.frame(
            Comparison = reordered_comparisons,
            Factor = factor,
            Continuous_Var = cont_var,
            Distribution = distribution_status,
            Variance = variance_status,
            Test = "Tukey's HSD (ANOVA)",
            P_Value = p_values,
            Significance = case_when(
              p_values <= 0.001 ~ "***",
              p_values <= 0.01 ~ "**",
              p_values <= 0.05 ~ "*",
              TRUE ~ "Not significant"
            )
          )

          results_list[[paste(cont_var, factor, sep = "_")]] <- sig_pairs
        } else {
          #if no valid groupings are present, return an empty dataframe
          results_list[[paste(cont_var, factor, sep = "_")]] <- data.frame(
            Comparison = NA,
            Factor = factor,
            Continuous_Var = cont_var,
            Distribution = distribution_status,
            Variance = variance_status,
            Test = "Tukey's HSD (No significant groupings)",
            P_Value = NA,
            Significance = "Not significant"
          )
        }
      } else {
        #Kruskal-Wallis and Dunn's Test for non-parametric data
        kruskal <- kruskal.test(as.formula(paste(cont_var, "~", factor)), data = filtered_data)

        if (kruskal$p.value < 0.05) { #Dunn's Test if Kruskal-Wallis is significant
          dunn <- dunn.test(filtered_data[[cont_var]], filtered_data[[factor]], method = "bonferroni", kw = FALSE)

          #calculate group medians for ordering comparisons
          group_medians <- tapply(filtered_data[[cont_var]], filtered_data[[factor]], median, na.rm = TRUE)
          
          comparisons <- dunn$comparisons
          p_values <- dunn$P.adjusted
          
          #reorder comparisons so higher median is listed first
          reordered_comparisons <- sapply(comparisons, function(comp) {
            groups <- strsplit(comp, " - ")[[1]]
            group1 <- trimws(groups[1])
            group2 <- trimws(groups[2])
            
            if (group_medians[group1] > group_medians[group2]) {
              paste(group1, ">", group2)
            } else {
              paste(group2, ">", group1)
            }
          })
          
          sig_pairs <- data.frame(
            Comparison = reordered_comparisons,
            Factor = factor,
            Continuous_Var = cont_var,
            Distribution = distribution_status,
            Variance = variance_status,
            Test = "Dunn's Test (Kruskal-Wallis)",
            P_Value = p_values,
            Significance = case_when(
              p_values <= 0.001 ~ "***",
              p_values <= 0.01 ~ "**",
              p_values <= 0.05 ~ "*",
              TRUE ~ "Not significant"
            )
          ) %>%
            filter(P_Value < 1)

          results_list[[paste(cont_var, factor, sep = "_")]] <- sig_pairs
        } else {
          results_list[[paste(cont_var, factor, sep = "_")]] <- data.frame(
            Comparison = NA,
            Factor = factor,
            Continuous_Var = cont_var,
            Distribution = distribution_status,
            Variance = variance_status,
            Test = "Kruskal-Wallis (NS)",
            P_Value = NA,
            Significance = "Not significant"
          )
        }
      }
    }
  }

  #combine results for all factors and continuous variables
  results_df <- bind_rows(results_list, .id = "Analysis_Combination")
  
  return(results_df)
}
```

```{r set up multifactoral/lme function}

#analysis function for multifactor models with interactions, Shapiro test, Levene test, Bartlett's test, group size evaluation, and NA omission
differences_multifactor <- function(data, factors, continuous_vars, random_var = NULL) {
  results_list <- list()

  for (cont_var in continuous_vars) {
    # Create formula with all factors and interactions
    factor_formula <- paste(factors, collapse = " * ")
    
    # Remove NA values for the current continuous variable and all factors
    cols_needed <- c(factors, cont_var)
    if (!is.null(random_var)) {
      cols_needed <- c(cols_needed, random_var)
    }
    filtered_data <- na.omit(data[, cols_needed])

    # Check if all groups for each factor have at least 2 observations
    insufficient_groups <- FALSE
    for (factor in factors) {
      group_sizes <- table(filtered_data[[factor]])
      if (any(group_sizes < 2)) {
        insufficient_groups <- TRUE
        break
      }
    }
    
    if (insufficient_groups) {
      # If any factor has groups with fewer than 2 observations, skip analysis and add a note
      results_list[[cont_var]] <- data.frame(
        Comparison = NA,
        Factors = paste(factors, collapse = " * "),
        Continuous_Var = cont_var,
        Distribution = "Skipped",
        Variance = "Skipped",
        Test = "Skipped (Insufficient group size)",
        P_Value = NA,
        Significance = "Not significant"
      )
      next
    }

    # Step 1: Test normality using Shapiro-Wilk test on residuals
    if (is.null(random_var)) {
      full_formula <- as.formula(paste(cont_var, "~", factor_formula))
      anova_res <- aov(full_formula, data = filtered_data)
    } else {
      full_formula <- as.formula(paste(cont_var, "~", factor_formula, "+ (1|", random_var, ")"))
      anova_res <- lme4::lmer(full_formula, data = filtered_data, REML = TRUE, na.action = na.omit)
    }
    
    residuals <- residuals(anova_res)
    shapiro <- shapiro.test(residuals)
    
    # Determine normality category
    if (shapiro$p.value > 0.05) {
      distribution_status <- "Normal"
    } else if (shapiro$statistic > 0.9) {
      distribution_status <- "Minor non-normality"
    } else {
      distribution_status <- "Major non-normality"
    }

    # Step 2: Test homogeneity of variances
    # Create interaction groups for both Bartlett and Levene tests
    if (length(factors) == 1) {
      interaction_groups <- filtered_data[[factors[1]]]
    } else if (length(factors) == 2) {
      interaction_groups <- interaction(filtered_data[[factors[1]]], filtered_data[[factors[2]]])
    } else if (length(factors) == 3) {
      interaction_groups <- interaction(filtered_data[[factors[1]]], filtered_data[[factors[2]]], filtered_data[[factors[3]]])
    }
    
    # Use Bartlett's test if normally distributed, Levene's test if not
    if (distribution_status == "Normal") {
      bartlett <- bartlett.test(filtered_data[[cont_var]], interaction_groups)
      variance_test_pvalue <- bartlett$p.value
    } else {
      levene <- car::leveneTest(filtered_data[[cont_var]], interaction_groups)
      variance_test_pvalue <- levene$`Pr(>F)`[1]
    }
    
    # Determine homogeneity status
    variance_status <- ifelse(variance_test_pvalue > 0.05, "Homogeneous", "Heterogeneous")

    # Step 3: Decide which statistical test to use
    # Parametric assumptions met: Normal distribution (or minor non-normality) AND homogeneous variances
    use_parametric <- (distribution_status %in% c("Normal", "Minor non-normality")) && (variance_status == "Homogeneous")

    if (use_parametric) {
      # Run Type III ANOVA
      if (is.null(random_var)) {
        full_formula <- as.formula(paste(cont_var, "~", factor_formula))
        lm_model <- lm(full_formula, data = filtered_data)
      } else {
        full_formula <- as.formula(paste(cont_var, "~", factor_formula, "+ (1|", random_var, ")"))
        lm_model <- lme4::lmer(full_formula, data = filtered_data, REML = TRUE, na.action = na.omit)
      }
      
      anova_results <- car::Anova(lm_model, type = 3)
      
      # Extract main effects and interactions from Type III ANOVA
      anova_df <- as.data.frame(anova_results)
      anova_df$Term <- rownames(anova_df)
      anova_df <- anova_df[!(rownames(anova_df) == "(Intercept)"), ] # Remove intercept
      
      for (idx in seq_len(nrow(anova_df))) {
        term_name <- anova_df$Term[idx]
        p_value <- anova_df$`Pr(>F)`[idx]
        
        sig_label <- case_when(
          p_value <= 0.001 ~ "***",
          p_value <= 0.01 ~ "**",
          p_value <= 0.05 ~ "*",
          TRUE ~ "Not significant"
        )
        
        results_list[[paste(cont_var, term_name, sep = "_")]] <- data.frame(
          Comparison = term_name,
          Factors = paste(factors, collapse = " * "),
          Continuous_Var = cont_var,
          Distribution = distribution_status,
          Variance = variance_status,
          Test = "Type III ANOVA",
          P_Value = p_value,
          Significance = sig_label
        )
      }
      
      # ANOVA and Tukey's HSD for pairwise comparisons
      if (is.null(random_var)) {
        full_formula <- as.formula(paste(cont_var, "~", factor_formula))
        anova_res <- aov(full_formula, data = filtered_data)
        tukey <- TukeyHSD(anova_res)
      } else {
        # For mixed models, use emmeans for post-hoc comparisons
        tukey_list <- list()
        for (factor in factors) {
          emmeans_result <- emmeans::emmeans(lm_model, as.formula(paste("~", factor)))
          tukey_list[[factor]] <- pairs(emmeans_result, adjust = "tukey")
        }
        tukey <- tukey_list
      }

      # Extract pairwise comparisons and P-values for each factor
      if (is.null(random_var)) {
        for (i in seq_along(tukey)) {
          factor_name <- names(tukey)[i]
          
          if (!is.null(tukey[[i]])) {
            # Calculate group means for ordering comparisons
            group_means <- tapply(filtered_data[[cont_var]], filtered_data[[factor_name]], mean, na.rm = TRUE)
            
            comparisons <- rownames(tukey[[i]])
            p_values <- tukey[[i]][, "p adj"]
            
            # Reorder comparisons so higher mean is listed first
            reordered_comparisons <- sapply(comparisons, function(comp) {
              groups <- strsplit(comp, "-")[[1]]
              group1 <- trimws(groups[1])
              group2 <- trimws(groups[2])
              
              if (group_means[group1] > group_means[group2]) {
                paste(group1, ">", group2)
              } else {
                paste(group2, ">", group1)
              }
            })
            
            sig_pairs <- data.frame(
              Comparison = reordered_comparisons,
              Factors = paste(factors, collapse = " * "),
              Continuous_Var = cont_var,
              Distribution = distribution_status,
              Variance = variance_status,
              Test = paste("Tukey's HSD -", factor_name),
              P_Value = p_values,
              Significance = case_when(
                p_values <= 0.001 ~ "***",
                p_values <= 0.01 ~ "**",
                p_values <= 0.05 ~ "*",
                TRUE ~ "Not significant"
              )
            )

            results_list[[paste(cont_var, "tukey", factor_name, sep = "_")]] <- sig_pairs
          }
        }
      } else {
        # For mixed models with emmeans
        for (factor in factors) {
          tukey_result <- tukey[[factor]]
          p_values <- tukey_result@test$p.value
          comparisons <- as.character(tukey_result@grid$contrast)
          
          # Calculate group means for ordering comparisons
          group_means <- tapply(filtered_data[[cont_var]], filtered_data[[factor]], mean, na.rm = TRUE)
          
          # Reorder comparisons so higher mean is listed first
          reordered_comparisons <- sapply(comparisons, function(comp) {
            groups <- strsplit(comp, " - ")[[1]]
            group1 <- trimws(groups[1])
            group2 <- trimws(groups[2])
            
            if (group_means[group1] > group_means[group2]) {
              paste(group1, ">", group2)
            } else {
              paste(group2, ">", group1)
            }
          })
          
          sig_pairs <- data.frame(
            Comparison = reordered_comparisons,
            Factors = paste(factors, collapse = " * "),
            Continuous_Var = cont_var,
            Distribution = distribution_status,
            Variance = variance_status,
            Test = paste("Tukey's HSD -", factor),
            P_Value = p_values,
            Significance = case_when(
              p_values <= 0.001 ~ "***",
              p_values <= 0.01 ~ "**",
              p_values <= 0.05 ~ "*",
              TRUE ~ "Not significant"
            )
          )
          
          results_list[[paste(cont_var, "tukey", factor, sep = "_")]] <- sig_pairs
        }
      }
    } else {
      # Run ART ANOVA for non-parametric
      # ARTool requires factors to be of class factor, not character
      art_data <- filtered_data
      for (factor in factors) {
        if (!is.factor(art_data[[factor]])) {
          art_data[[factor]] <- as.factor(art_data[[factor]])
        }
      }
      
      # Create the formula and run ART
      full_formula <- as.formula(paste(cont_var, "~", factor_formula))
      art_result <- ARTool::art(full_formula, data = art_data)
      
      # Extract ART ANOVA results
      art_anova <- anova(art_result)
      art_df <- as.data.frame(art_anova)
      art_df$Term <- rownames(art_df)
      
      for (idx in seq_len(nrow(art_df))) {
        term_name <- art_df$Term[idx]
        p_value <- art_df$`Pr(>F)`[idx]
        
        sig_label <- case_when(
          p_value <= 0.001 ~ "***",
          p_value <= 0.01 ~ "**",
          p_value <= 0.05 ~ "*",
          TRUE ~ "Not significant"
        )
        
        results_list[[paste(cont_var, "art", term_name, sep = "_")]] <- data.frame(
          Comparison = term_name,
          Factors = paste(factors, collapse = " * "),
          Continuous_Var = cont_var,
          Distribution = distribution_status,
          Variance = variance_status,
          Test = "ART ANOVA",
          P_Value = p_value,
          Significance = sig_label
        )
      }
      
      # Kruskal-Wallis and Dunn's Test for pairwise comparisons
      for (factor in factors) {
        kruskal <- kruskal.test(as.formula(paste(cont_var, "~", factor)), data = filtered_data)

        if (kruskal$p.value < 0.05) { # Dunn's Test if Kruskal-Wallis is significant
          dunn <- dunn.test(filtered_data[[cont_var]], filtered_data[[factor]], method = "bonferroni", kw = FALSE)

          # Calculate group medians for ordering comparisons
          group_medians <- tapply(filtered_data[[cont_var]], filtered_data[[factor]], median, na.rm = TRUE)
          
          comparisons <- dunn$comparisons
          p_values <- dunn$P.adjusted
          
          # Reorder comparisons so higher median is listed first
          reordered_comparisons <- sapply(comparisons, function(comp) {
            groups <- strsplit(comp, " - ")[[1]]
            group1 <- trimws(groups[1])
            group2 <- trimws(groups[2])
            
            if (group_medians[group1] > group_medians[group2]) {
              paste(group1, ">", group2)
            } else {
              paste(group2, ">", group1)
            }
          })
          
          sig_pairs <- data.frame(
            Comparison = reordered_comparisons,
            Factors = paste(factors, collapse = " * "),
            Continuous_Var = cont_var,
            Distribution = distribution_status,
            Variance = variance_status,
            Test = paste("Dunn's Test -", factor),
            P_Value = p_values,
            Significance = case_when(
              p_values <= 0.001 ~ "***",
              p_values <= 0.01 ~ "**",
              p_values <= 0.05 ~ "*",
              TRUE ~ "Not significant"
            )
          ) %>%
            filter(P_Value < 1)

          results_list[[paste(cont_var, "dunn", factor, sep = "_")]] <- sig_pairs
        } else {
          results_list[[paste(cont_var, "dunn", factor, sep = "_")]] <- data.frame(
            Comparison = NA,
            Factors = paste(factors, collapse = " * "),
            Continuous_Var = cont_var,
            Distribution = distribution_status,
            Variance = variance_status,
            Test = paste("Kruskal-Wallis (NS) -", factor),
            P_Value = NA,
            Significance = "Not significant"
          )
        }
      }
    }
  }

  # Combine results for all factors and continuous variables
  results_df <- bind_rows(results_list, .id = "Analysis_Combination")
  
  return(results_df)
}
```

```{r load plant harvest data}

#read in 13C initial harvest data
harvest <- read_csv("Stagg_harvest.csv") %>% #load
  clean_names() #clean up column names

#pivot and calculate root:shoot ratio
plant_harvest <- harvest %>%
  mutate(across(c(8:17), as.numeric)) %>% #convert columns to numeric
  dplyr::select(site, site_id, management, pot, species, functional_group, sample_type, biomass_g) %>%
  filter(biomass_g >= 0) %>% #remove non-plant data
  group_by(site, site_id, management, pot, species, functional_group, sample_type) %>%
  summarise(biomass_g = mean(biomass_g, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = 'drop') %>% #summarize duplicate entries for groups
  pivot_wider(names_from = sample_type, values_from = biomass_g) %>% #determines observation name and value columns
  mutate(root_shoot = #calculate root:shoot ratio
           case_when(root > 0 & shoot > 0 ~ root / shoot, #when values are present
                     TRUE ~ NA)) %>% #default to NA when values are not present
  mutate(harvesttime = #define harvest time
        case_when(pot == "G1" | pot == "G20" | pot == "G30" | pot == "G31" | pot == "G39" |
                  pot == "G8" | pot == "G33" | pot == "G35" | pot == "G41" | pot == "G42" |
                  pot == "G9" | pot == "G12" | pot == "G22" | pot == "GA1" | pot == "GA2" |
                  pot == "G11" | pot == "G18" | pot == "G29" | pot == "GF1" | pot == "GX"
                  ~ "T0", #time 0 beginning of incubation
                     TRUE ~ "T10mos")) #10 months incubation

#summarize biomass for plots

  dplyr::select(site, site_id, management, species, functional_group, shoot, root, root_shoot) %>%
  group_by(site, management, species, functional_group) %>%
  summarise(across(where(is.numeric), summary_stats)) #run all summary stats

#summarize biomass by plant species for estimates

  dplyr::select(species, functional_group, shoot, root, root_shoot) %>%
  group_by(species, functional_group) %>%
  summarise(across(where(is.numeric), summary_stats)) #run all summary stats

#13C calculations

                     [match(paste(site, sample_type), 
                            paste(nat_abun$site, nat_abun$sample_type))], TRUE ~ NA)) %>% 
  mutate(excess13C_mg = case_when(sample_type == "shoot" | sample_type == "root"

#summarize means 13C for plots - by species

  group_by(site, site_id, sample_type, species, functional_group) %>%

#summarize 13C for plots add up - by site and type only

           case_when(root > 0 ~ root,
                     TRUE ~ root_shoot * shoot))
is.na(plant_harvest_est) <- sapply(plant_harvest_est, is.nan) #replace NaN with NA for better handling of missing data

#summarize general roots amount by site
general_roots <- plant_harvest_est %>%
  filter(species == "general_roots") %>%
  dplyr::select(site2, root) %>%
  group_by(site2) %>%
  summarise(across(where(is.numeric), summary_stats)) #run all summary stats

#calculate and estimate biomass per pot
total_pots <- plant_harvest_est %>%
  dplyr::select(site2, management, pot, harvesttime, root, shoot, root_shoot) %>%
  group_by(site2, management, pot, harvesttime) %>%
  summarise(root = sum(root, na.rm=TRUE), shoot = sum(shoot, na.rm=TRUE), root_shoot = mean(root_shoot, na.rm=TRUE)) %>% #summarize
  mutate(root = #add some general roots to the estimated beginning biomass for incubation
           dplyr::case_when(harvesttime == "T0" ~ root,
                     TRUE ~ root + general_roots$root_mean[match(site2, general_roots$site2)])) #+
                     #general_roots$sd[match(site2, general_roots$site2)]))

#write csv for measured and estimated beginning biomass
#write.csv(plant_harvest_est, "begin_estimates_bysp.csv") #saves as csv in current workspace
#write.csv(total_pots, "begin_estimates_bypot.csv") #saves as csv in current workspace

#order variables
plant_harvest$site <- factor(plant_harvest$site, levels = order_sites)
plant_harvest$site_id <- factor(plant_harvest$site_id, levels = order_IDs)
plant_harvest_est$site <- factor(plant_harvest_est$site, levels = order_sites)
plant_harvest_est$site_id <- factor(plant_harvest_est$site_id, levels = order_IDs)
plant13C$site <- factor(plant13C$site, levels = order_sites)
plant13C$site_id <- factor(plant13C$site_id, levels = order_IDs)
summary_plant13C$site <- factor(summary_plant13C$site, levels = order_sites)
summary_plant13C$site_id <- factor(summary_plant13C$site_id, levels = order_IDs)

```

```{r calc plant biodiversity}

#Pivot data to wide format
species_df_wide <- plant_harvest %>%
  dplyr::select(pot, species, shoot) %>% #select only needed columns
  filter(!is.na(species) & !grepl("general_roots", species)) %>% #remove any NA species
  pivot_wider(names_from = species, values_from = shoot) %>% #determines observation name and value columns
  replace(is.na(.), 0) %>% #make any missing values 0
  column_to_rownames(var="pot") #sets observation column as row names

#Calculate species richness, Shannon index, and Simpson index with vegan library
species_richness <- specnumber(species_df_wide) #calculate species richness
shannon <- diversity(species_df_wide, index = "shannon") #calculate Shannon index
simpson <- diversity(species_df_wide, index = "simpson") #calculate Simpson index

#Combine biodiversity metrics into a dataframe
diversity <- data.frame(
  pot = rownames(species_df_wide), #put observations back into column
  species_richness = species_richness,
  shannon = shannon,
  simpson = simpson,
  row.names = NULL
) 

diversity <- diversity %>%
  mutate(site_id = plant_harvest$site_id[match(diversity$pot, plant_harvest$pot)]) %>% #add site information back in
  mutate(site = plant_harvest$site[match(diversity$pot, plant_harvest$pot)])

```

```{r load AM and biomass fungi data}
#read in AM association data
AMdata <- read_csv("Wigan_myc.csv")

#order variables

AMdata$Mgmt_fct <- factor(AMdata$Mgmt_fct, levels = order_mgmt)

#read in HLD data
HLD <- read_csv("HLD_Wigan.csv")

#order variables
HLD$Site_ID <- factor(HLD$Site_ID, levels = order_IDs)

#calculate fungal biomass C
HLD <- HLD %>%
  mutate(other_biomass_gkg = other_sm_biomass_gkg + other_lg_biomass_gkg) %>%
  mutate(AM_C_mgkg = AM_biomass_gkg * 0.3 * 1000) %>% #use 30% C (Hodge and Fitter 2010, Zhang et al. 2025b), convert to mg per kg soil
  mutate(otherfun_C_mgkg = other_biomass_gkg * 0.41 * 1000) %>% #use 41% C (Pánek et al. 2024)
  mutate(total_fun_C_mgkg = AM_C_mgkg + otherfun_C_mgkg) #add together

#melt to be able to stack a bar chart for biomass
fungal_mass <- HLD %>%
  dplyr::select(Site_ID, AM_biomass_gkg, other_biomass_gkg) %>%
  pivot_longer(
		cols = AM_biomass_gkg:other_biomass_gkg, #pick columns
		names_to = "fungal_type", #name column to put original column names in
		values_to = "g_biomass") #name column to put values in

#melt to be able to stack a bar chart for biomass C
fungal_C <- HLD %>%
  dplyr::select(Site_ID, AM_C_mgkg, otherfun_C_mgkg) %>%
  pivot_longer(
		cols = AM_C_mgkg:otherfun_C_mgkg, #pick columns
		names_to = "fungal_type", #name column to put original column names in
		values_to = "mg_C") #name column to put values in
```

### Soil organic matter

```{r load Kimpton SOM data, eval=FALSE}

#read in field soil C/N data
SOM_Kimpton <- read_csv("SOM_Kimpton.csv") 

#Combine SOM, POM, and MAOM as one observation per plot
SOM <- SOM_Kimpton %>%
  filter(Fraction == "SOM") %>%
  rename("SOM_C" = "C_gkg") %>%
  rename("SOM_N" = "N_gkg") %>%
  rename("SOM_CN" = "C_N") %>%
  rename("SOM_C_kgm2_7cm" = "C_kgm2_7cm")

POM <- SOM_Kimpton %>%
  filter(Fraction == "POM") %>%
  rename("POM_C" = "C_gkg") %>%
  rename("POM_N" = "N_gkg") %>%
  rename("POM_CN" = "C_N") %>%
  rename("POM_C_kgm2_7cm" = "C_kgm2_7cm")
  
MAOM <- SOM_Kimpton %>%
  filter(Fraction == "MAOM") %>%
  rename("MAOM_C" = "C_gkg") %>%
  rename("MAOM_N" = "N_gkg") %>%
  rename("MAOM_CN" = "C_N") %>%
  rename("MAOM_C_kgm2_7cm" = "C_kgm2_7cm")

SOM_Kimpton2 <- merge(MAOM,POM, by=c("Sample_year", "Site", "Site_ID", "Mgmt_year", "Plot_ID"), all.y=TRUE) %>%
  merge(SOM, by=c("Sample_year", "Site", "Site_ID", "Mgmt_year", "Plot_ID"), all.y=TRUE) %>%
  dplyr::select(Sample_year, Site_ID, Site, Mgmt_year, 
                SOM_C, SOM_N, SOM_CN, POM_C, POM_N, POM_CN, MAOM_C, MAOM_N, MAOM_CN,
                C_gcm3, C_Tha, SOM_C_kgm2_7cm, POM_C_kgm2_7cm, MAOM_C_kgm2_7cm) %>%
  mutate(fMAOM_C = MAOM_C_kgm2_7cm / (POM_C_kgm2_7cm + MAOM_C_kgm2_7cm)) %>% #calculate fMAOM C
  mutate(fMAOM_C_2 = MAOM_C_kgm2_7cm / SOM_C_kgm2_7cm) %>% #calculate fMAOM C
  mutate(fMAOM_N = MAOM_N / (POM_N + MAOM_N)) %>% #calculate fMAOM N
  mutate(fMAOM_N_2 = MAOM_N / SOM_N) #calculate fMAOM N

#remove SOM, POM, and MAOM dataframes to clean up environment
rm(SOM, POM, MAOM)

#summarize SOM data for plots
summary_SOM_Kimpton <- SOM_Kimpton2 %>%
  group_by(Sample_year, Site, Site_ID, Mgmt_year) %>%
  summarise(across(where(is.numeric), summary_stats)) #run all summary stats

#order variables
SOM_Kimpton$Site <- factor(SOM_Kimpton$Site, levels = order_sites)
SOM_Kimpton2$Site <- factor(SOM_Kimpton2$Site, levels = order_sites)
summary_SOM_Kimpton$Site <- factor(summary_SOM_Kimpton$Site, levels = order_sites)
```

```{r load SOM-13C data}
  rename("POM_15N" = "15N") %>%
  rename("POM_C_kgm2_7cm" = "C_kgm2_7cm")
  
MAOM_T0 <- SOM_13C %>%
  filter(Fraction == "MAOM") %>%
  filter(Incubation_T == 0) %>%
  dplyr::select(Sample_year, Site_ID, Site, Mgmt_year, Mgmt_fct, Plot_ID, Incubation_T, per_C, per_N, C_gkg, N_gkg, C_N, d13C, `13C_excess_per`, `15N`, per_POM, per_MAOM, C_kgm2_7cm, pot_C_g, pot_13C_mg) %>% #select columns to keep
  rename("MAOM_perC" = "per_C") %>%
  rename("MAOM_perN" = "per_N") %>%
  rename("MAOM_potC_g" = "pot_C_g") %>%
  rename("MAOM_C" = "C_gkg") %>%
  rename("MAOM_N" = "N_gkg") %>%
  rename("MAOM_CN" = "C_N")  %>%
  rename("MAOM_d13C" = "d13C") %>%
  rename("MAOM_13C_excess" = "13C_excess_per") %>%
  rename("MAOM_pot13C_mg" = "pot_13C_mg") %>%
  rename("MAOM_15N" = "15N") %>%
  rename("MAOM_C_kgm2_7cm" = "C_kgm2_7cm")

SOM_13C_T0 <- merge(SOM_T0, POM_T0, by=c("Sample_year", "Site", "Site_ID", "Mgmt_year", "Mgmt_fct", "Plot_ID", "Incubation_T"), all=TRUE) %>%
  merge(MAOM_T0, by=c("Sample_year", "Site", "Site_ID", "Mgmt_year", "Mgmt_fct", "Plot_ID", "Incubation_T"), all.y=TRUE) %>%
  mutate(fMAOM_C = MAOM_C_kgm2_7cm / (POM_C_kgm2_7cm + MAOM_C_kgm2_7cm)) %>% #calculate fMAOM C
  mutate(fMAOM_C_2 = MAOM_C_kgm2_7cm / SOM_C_kgm2_7cm) %>% #calculate fMAOM C
  mutate(fMAOM_13C = MAOM_pot13C_mg / (MAOM_pot13C_mg + POM_pot13C_mg)) %>% #calculate fMAOM 13C
  mutate(M13C_P13C = MAOM_pot13C_mg / POM_pot13C_mg) %>% #calculate ratio transfer to MAOM vs POM
  mutate(fMAOM_N = MAOM_N / (POM_N + MAOM_N)) %>% #calculate fMAOM N
  mutate(fMAOM_N_2 = MAOM_N / SOM_N) #calculate fMAOM N

#remove SOM, POM, and MAOM dataframes to clean up environment
rm(SOM_T0, POM_T0, MAOM_T0)
```

```{r load 2026 SOM data}

#read in field soil C/N data from 2026 and calculate additional
SOM_2026 <- read_csv("SOM_2026.csv") %>%
  rename("SOM_C_kgm2_7cm" = "C_kgm2_7cm") %>%
  mutate(MAOM_perC = 
           MAOM53_perC*(per_53/(per_53+per_45)) + MAOM45_perC*(per_45/(per_53+per_45))) %>% #calculate total MAOM per C
  mutate(MAOM_perN = 
           MAOM53_perN*(per_53/(per_53+per_45)) + MAOM45_perN*(per_45/(per_53+per_45))) %>% #calculate total MAOM per N
  mutate(MAOM_CN = MAOM_perC / MAOM_perN) %>% #calculate total MAOM C/N
  mutate(MAOM45_C_kgm2_7cm = ((MAOM45_perC/100) * per_45 * adj_BD * (10/1000) * 10000 * 0.7)) %>% #calculate MAOM45 C per km2 to 7cm depth
  mutate(MAOM53_C_kgm2_7cm = ((MAOM53_perC/100) * per_53 * adj_BD * (10/1000) * 10000 * 0.7)) %>% #calculate MAOM53 C per km2 to 7cm depth
  mutate(MAOM_C_kgm2_7cm = ((MAOM_perC/100) * per_MAOM * adj_BD * (10/1000) * 10000 * 0.7)) %>%
  mutate(POM_C_kgm2_7cm = ((POM_perC/100) * per_POM * adj_BD * (10/1000) * 10000 * 0.7)) %>%
  mutate(POM53_perC = 
           POM_perC*(per_POM/(per_53+per_POM)) + MAOM53_perC*(per_53/(per_53+per_POM))) %>% #calculate POM C including the <53>45 um fraction
  mutate(per_POM53 = per_POM + per_53) %>% #calculate percentage of POM including the <53>45 um fraction
  mutate(POM53_C_kgm2_7cm = ((POM53_perC/100) * per_POM53 * adj_BD * (10/1000) * 10000 * 0.7)) %>%
  mutate(fMAOM_C = MAOM_C_kgm2_7cm / (POM_C_kgm2_7cm + MAOM_C_kgm2_7cm)) #calculate fMAOM C

#summarize SOM 2026 data 
summary_SOM_2026 <- SOM_2026[c(3:7,10,14,26,29,30:32,35:56)] %>%
  group_by(Site_ID, Site, Mgmt_year, Management) %>%

  bind_rows(SOM_2026)
```

```{r load UK data}
#load dataset UK grasslands - from DRYAD repository, Manning et al. 2016
UK_soil <- read_csv("Manning2015_dryad.csv") %>%

  mutate(MAOM_C = C50_0.45) %>% #match to Wigan data

  mutate(vegetation = str_replace(vegetation, "wet grassland", "Wet Grassland")) %>% #match naming with Wigan data
  mutate(vegetation = str_replace(vegetation, "Acid grass", "Acid Grass")) %>% #match naming with Wigan data
  mutate(Sample_year = 2005) %>%
  dplyr::select(Sample_year, vegetation, type, site, pH, TotalC, POM_C, MAOM_C) %>%

  summarise(across(pH:MAOM_C, list(mean = ~ mean(., na.rm=TRUE),
```

### Incubation biomass decomposition

```{r load incubation biomass data}

#read in incubation data, add beginning, calculate change in biomass
endbiomass <- read_csv("End_incubation_biomass.csv") %>% #load
  mutate(est_beg_drymass = total_pots$root[match(Pot, total_pots$pot)]) %>% #add estimated beginning biomass
  mutate(beg_drymass_perL = est_beg_drymass / 6.1) %>% #calculate dry mass per liter
  mutate(dmass_dT = est_beg_drymass - end_drymass_clean) %>% #calculate change in dry mass
  mutate(dmass_dT_perL = beg_drymass_perL - end_drymass_perL_clean) %>% #calculate change in dry mass per liter
  mutate(decomp_per_unadj = dmass_dT / est_beg_drymass) %>% #calculate decomposition percentage - not adjusting volume
  mutate(decomp_per_adj = dmass_dT_perL / beg_drymass_perL) %>% #calculate decomposition percentage - adjusting volume
  mutate(years =
           case_when(Management == "Unmanaged" ~ 0,
                     Management == "4 Years" ~ 4,
                     Management == "15 Years" ~ 15,
                     Management == "23 Years" ~ 23))

#Add data
endbiomass <- endbiomass %>%
  mutate(AM_hyph_per = AMdata$hyph_percent[match(endbiomass$Pot, AMdata$Plot_ID)]) %>%
  mutate(AM_hyph_ct = AMdata$Hyphae[match(endbiomass$Pot, AMdata$Plot_ID)]) %>%
  mutate(AM_arb_per = AMdata$arbuscule_percent[match(endbiomass$Pot, AMdata$Plot_ID)]) %>%
  mutate(AM_arb_ct = AMdata$Arbuscule[match(endbiomass$Pot, AMdata$Plot_ID)]) %>%
  mutate(AM_ves_ct = AMdata$Vesicle[match(endbiomass$Pot, AMdata$Plot_ID)]) %>%
  mutate(AM_absent = AMdata$Nothing[match(endbiomass$Pot, AMdata$Plot_ID)]) %>%
  mutate(pH = SOM_13C_T0$pH <- site_data$pH[match(endbiomass$Pot, site_data$Plot_ID)]) %>%
  mutate(pH_range = case_when(pH <= 5 ~ "Very Strongly Acidic",
                                pH > 5 & pH <= 5.5 ~ "Strongly Acidic",
                                pH > 5.5 & pH <= 6 ~ "Moderately Acidic",
                                pH > 6 & pH <= 6.5 ~ "Mildly Acidic",
                                pH > 6.5 & pH <= 7.3 ~ "Neutral",
                                pH > 7.3 ~ "Alkaline"))


#summarise
summary_endbio <- endbiomass %>%
  dplyr::select(Site, Site_ID, Management, years, rocks_debris, end_drymass_clean, end_drymass_perL_clean, est_beg_drymass, beg_drymass_perL, decomp_per_adj) %>%
  group_by(Site, Site_ID, Management, years) %>%
  summarise(across(where(is.numeric), summary_stats)) #run all summary stats

#order variables
```

### Sites

```{r map sites}

library(tmap) #background map

#create df with site locations
site_locations <- data.frame(
  Site_ID = order_IDs,
  #order = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6),
  long = c(-2.542323, -2.540316, -2.591300, -2.593789, -2.627059, -2.623926),
  lat = c(53.508020, 53.504838, 53.527421, 53.526987, 53.525431, 53.524940)
)

#define the bounding box and center points for Wigan
bbox <- c(xmin = -2.63, ymin = 53.501, xmax = -2.536, ymax = 53.53)

#convert to sf object and specify order
locations_sf <- st_as_sf(site_locations, coords = c("long", "lat"), crs = 4326)
locations_sf$Site_ID <- factor(locations_sf$Site_ID, levels = order_IDs)

#create map with tmap library
tm_basemap("OpenStreetMap", alpha = 0.9) +
  tm_shape(locations_sf, bbox = bbox) +
  tm_squares(size = 0.8, #create points, define shape and size
             plot.order = tm_plot_order("DATA"), #define order
             fill = "Site_ID", fill.scale = tm_scale(values = colors6), #fill variable and colors
             fill.legend = tm_legend(title = "Site", position = c("right", "top"))) + #legend
  tm_text("Site_ID", ymod = -0.8) #, xmod = 1) #set label locations
  
#save figure
tmap_save(filename = "Figures/Sites_map.png", width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 300)



```


## Soil properties
```{r soil char}

#soil pH differences - 2023 data
shapiro.test(resid(lm(pH ~ Management, data = site_data))) #check normality of residuals - not normal
kruskal.test(pH ~ Management, data = site_data) #Kruskal-Wallis test - significant
dunn.test(site_data$pH, site_data$Management, method = "bonferroni", kw=TRUE) #23 yr vs. 4 and 0, 15 vs. 4

#soil bulk density differences - 2026 data
shapiro.test(resid(lm(adj_BD ~ Management * Site, data = SOM_2026))) #check normality of residuals - normal
summary(aov(adj_BD ~ Management * Site, data = SOM_2026)) #ANOVA - none significant


```

## FTIR compounds

```{r FTIR stats}

#define what to analyze for differences
factors <- "site_id" #predictor variable
continuous_vars <- c("x907", "x1002", "x1402", "x1630", "x794", "x2846", "x2937", "x3620") #response variables
data <- FTIR %>%
  clean_names()

#evaluate group sizes
evaluate_group_sizes(data, factors, continuous_vars) 

#eun the analysis
FTIR_diff <- differences_function(data, factors, continuous_vars)

#aromatic:aliphatic ratio
FTIR_stbl_lbl <- FTIR %>%
  clean_names() %>%
  group_by(site) %>%
  mutate(ar_al = (x794)/(x1402)) %>%
  mutate(stbl_lbl = (x794+x2846+x2937)/(x907+x1002+x1402)) 

FTIR_summary <- FTIR_stbl_lbl %>%
  summarise(across(ar_al:stbl_lbl, list(mean = ~ mean(., na.rm=TRUE),
                                 sd = ~ sd(., na.rm=TRUE),
                                 se = ~ std.error(., na.rm=TRUE))))

shapiro.test(resid(lm(ar_al ~ site_id, data = FTIR_stbl_lbl))) #check normality of residuals - normal
bartlett.test(ar_al ~ site_id, data = FTIR_stbl_lbl)
summary(aov(ar_al ~ site_id, data = FTIR_stbl_lbl)) #ANOVA - significant
TukeyHSD(aov(ar_al ~ site_id, data = FTIR_stbl_lbl)) #Flashes vs. all, Amberswood vs. Bickershaw 1

```

```{r FTIR PCA}

#PCA
FTIR_pca <- prcomp(FTIR_standardized_num) #perform PCA on standardized variables

summary(FTIR_pca) #view importance of principal components and proportion of variances

FTIR_pca$rotation #view loadings from the standardized data
screeplot(FTIR_pca) # diagnostic plot to make sure principal components are in order

#basic plot
biplot(FTIR_pca)

#customized plot
autoplot(FTIR_pca, data = FTIR_standardized, colour = 'Site_ID', fill = 'Site_ID',
         loadings = TRUE, loadings.colour = 'black',
         loadings.label = TRUE, loadings.label.size = 3,
         frame = TRUE, frame.type = 'norm', frame.colour = 'Site_ID', frame.fill = 'Site_ID',
         shape = 21) +
  scale_color_manual(values = colors4) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = colors4) +
  my_theme +
  ggtitle("Principal Components of FTIR Wavelengths Across Sites")
```

## SOM Stats

### Compare years

```{r SOM years only}

#match data
SOM_multiyr_match <- SOM_multiyr %>%
  filter(Site_ID != "AU" & Site_ID != "FU") %>%
  mutate(Site_ID = droplevels(Site_ID)) %>% #drop unused factor levels
  mutate(Sample_yr_ch = paste0("_", Sample_year)) #force to character variable (as.factor and as.character weren't working)

#define what to analyze
factors <- "Sample_yr_ch" #predictor variable
continuous_vars <- c("SOM_perC", "SOM_C_kgm2_7cm", "SOM_perN", "SOM_CN",
                     "POM_perC", "POM_C_kgm2_7cm", "POM_perN",
                     "MAOM_perC", "MAOM_C_kgm2_7cm", "MAOM_perN", "fMAOM_C") #response variables
data <- SOM_multiyr_match

#evaluate group sizes
evaluate_group_sizes(data, factors, continuous_vars) 
summarize_group_sizes(data, factors, continuous_vars) 

#run the analysis
SOMyr_diff <- differences(data, factors, continuous_vars)

#filter only significant
SOMyr_sigdiff <- SOMyr_diff %>%
  filter(P_Value <= 0.05)



```

```{r SOM years sites}

#test for year and site
factors <- c("Site_ID", "Sample_yr_ch")
continuous_vars <- c("SOM_perC", "SOM_C_kgm2_7cm", "SOM_perN", "SOM_CN",
                     "POM_perC", "POM_C_kgm2_7cm", "POM_perN",
                     "MAOM_perC", "MAOM_C_kgm2_7cm", "MAOM_perN", "fMAOM_C") #response variables
data <- SOM_multiyr_match

SOMyrsite_diff <- differences_multifactor(data, factors, continuous_vars)

#test one set to make sure same results
#diagnostics
shapiro.test(resid(lm(SOM_perC ~ Sample_year * Site_ID, data = SOM_multiyr_match))) #almost normal
leveneTest(lm(SOM_perC ~ Sample_yr_ch * Site_ID, data = SOM_multiyr_match)) #heterogenous

#non-parametric
anova(art(SOM_perC ~ factor(Sample_yr_ch) * Site_ID, data = SOM_multiyr_match)) #ART ANOVA
scheirerRayHare(SOM_perC ~ factor(Sample_yr_ch) * Site_ID, data = SOM_multiyr_match) #SRH alternative to ART
dunn.test(SOM_multiyr_match$SOM_perC, c(factor(SOM_multiyr_match$Sample_yr_ch), SOM_multiyr_match$Site_ID), method="bonferroni", kw=TRUE)

#compare parametric - same outcomes
summary(aov(SOM_perC ~ Sample_year * Site_ID, data = SOM_multiyr_match)) 
TukeyHSD(aov(SOM_perC ~ factor(Sample_year) + Site_ID, data = SOM_multiyr_match)) 


#Calculate means to compare differences between years
SOM_multiyr_diff <- SOM_multiyr_match %>%
  dplyr::select(Sample_year, Site_ID, SOM_perC, POM_perC, MAOM_perC, SOM_C_kgm2_7cm, POM_C_kgm2_7cm, MAOM_C_kgm2_7cm) %>%
  group_by(Sample_year, Site_ID) %>%
  summarise(across(where(is.numeric), list(mean = ~mean(., na.rm=TRUE)))) #run all summary stats

#Calculate differences between years for each site and fraction
SOM_multiyr_diff <- SOM_multiyr_diff %>%
  group_by(Sample_year, Site_ID) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(SOM_perC_mean, POM_perC_mean, MAOM_perC_mean, SOM_C_kgm2_7cm_mean, POM_C_kgm2_7cm_mean, MAOM_C_kgm2_7cm_mean), names_to = "Fraction", values_to = "Value") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Sample_year, values_from = Value) %>%
  mutate(Diff = `2026` - `2023`) 


```


### Log response ratio cutting

```{r hay cutting SOM}

#unmanaged only means
avg_unmg_SOM <- SOM_2026 %>%
  filter(Management == "Unmanaged") %>%
  group_by(Site) %>%
  summarise(across(where(is.numeric), mean)) #get mean


#log response ratio of soil C
LRR_SOM_C <- SOM_2026 %>%
  dplyr::select(Site, Management, SOM_perC, SOM_C_Tha) %>%
  filter(Management == "Hay cutting") %>%
  mutate(SOM_perC_unmg = #add column for unmanaged means
           case_when(Site == "Bickershaw"
                     ~ avg_unmg_SOM$SOM_perC[avg_unmg_SOM$Site == "Bickershaw"],
                     Site == "Amberswood"
                     ~ avg_unmg_SOM$SOM_perC[avg_unmg_SOM$Site == "Amberswood"],
                     Site == "Flashes" 
                     ~ avg_unmg_SOM$SOM_perC[avg_unmg_SOM$Site == "Flashes"])) %>%
  mutate(LRR_SOM_perC = 
           log(SOM_perC/SOM_perC_unmg)) %>% #calculate log response ratio percent C
  mutate(SOM_CTha_unmg = #add column for unmanaged means
           case_when(Site == "Bickershaw"
                     ~ avg_unmg_SOM$SOM_C_Tha[avg_unmg_SOM$Site == "Bickershaw"],
                     Site == "Amberswood"
                     ~ avg_unmg_SOM$SOM_C_Tha[avg_unmg_SOM$Site == "Amberswood"],
                     Site == "Flashes" 
                     ~ avg_unmg_SOM$SOM_C_Tha[avg_unmg_SOM$Site == "Flashes"])) %>%
  mutate(LRR_SOM_CTha = 
           log(SOM_C_Tha/SOM_CTha_unmg)) #calculate log response ratio percent C

#calculate confidence intervals for log response ratios
predict(lm(LRR_SOM_perC ~ Site, data = LRR_SOM_C), interval = "confidence") #calculate confidence intervals for log response ratio of percent C
predict(lm(LRR_SOM_CTha ~ Site, data = LRR_SOM_C), interval = "confidence") #calculate confidence intervals for log response ratio of C in T ha

#plot log response ratios with confidence intervals in ggplot
ggplot(LRR_SOM_C, aes(y=Site, x=LRR_SOM_perC, fill=Site, color=Site)) +
  geom_point(size=2) +
  #geom_violin(alpha=0.2) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(xmin=predict(lm(LRR_SOM_perC ~ Site, data = LRR_SOM_C), 
                                 interval = "confidence")[,2],
                    xmax=predict(lm(LRR_SOM_perC ~ Site, data = LRR_SOM_C), 
                                 interval = "confidence")[,3]),
                width=0.2) +
  scale_color_manual(values = colors3) + scale_fill_manual(values = colors3) +
  #ggtitle("Log Response Ratio of SOM %C for Hay Cutting vs Unmanaged") +
  ylab("") + xlab("Log Response Ratio of SOM %C") +
  my_theme

#save plot
ggsave('LRR_SOM_perC.svg', #save plot name and type - can be "eps", "pdf", "jpeg", "tiff", "png", "bmp", "svg"
	path = "Figures", #save to folder within working directory
	width = 6, height = 3, units = "in", #set dimensions for figure
	dpi = 300, #set resolution
	bg=NULL) #background from plot specifications


```

### Compare with UK-wide unimproved grasslands soil C
```{r SOC compare}

shapiro.test(resid(lm(TotalC ~ type, data = soilC_compare))) #check normality of residuals - not normal
shapiro.test(resid(lm(log(TotalC) ~ type, data = soilC_compare))) #not normal, closer
summary(aov(log(TotalC) ~ type, data = soilC_compare)) #very sig

shapiro.test(resid(lm(TotalC ~ vegetation, data = soilC_compare))) #check normality of residuals - not normal
shapiro.test(resid(lm(log(TotalC) ~ vegetation, data = soilC_compare))) #not normal
summary(aov(log(TotalC) ~ vegetation, data = soilC_compare)) #very sig
TukeyHSD(aov(log(TotalC) ~ vegetation, data = soilC_compare)) #FM > mesotrophic

shapiro.test(resid(lm(POM_C ~ type, data = soilC_compare))) #check normality of residuals - not normal
shapiro.test(resid(lm(log(POM_C) ~ type, data = soilC_compare))) #normal
summary(aov(log(POM_C) ~ type, data = soilC_compare)) #not sig

shapiro.test(resid(lm(POM_C ~ vegetation, data = soilC_compare))) #check normality of residuals - not normal
shapiro.test(resid(lm(log(POM_C) ~ vegetation, data = soilC_compare))) #normal
summary(aov(log(POM_C) ~ vegetation, data = soilC_compare)) #very sig
TukeyHSD(aov(log(POM_C) ~ vegetation, data = soilC_compare)) #FM > mesotrophic, BU < wet

shapiro.test(resid(lm(MAOM_C ~ type, data = soilC_compare))) #not normal but W close to 1
shapiro.test(resid(lm(log(MAOM_C) ~ type, data = soilC_compare))) #not normal, worse
summary(aov(MAOM_C ~ type, data = soilC_compare)) #sig

shapiro.test(resid(lm(MAOM_C ~ vegetation, data = soilC_compare))) #not normal but W close to 1
shapiro.test(resid(lm(log(MAOM_C) ~ vegetation, data = soilC_compare))) #not normal, worse
summary(aov(MAOM_C ~ vegetation, data = soilC_compare)) #very sig
TukeyHSD(aov(MAOM_C ~ vegetation, data = soilC_compare)) #
```

```{r AM assoc waste 1}
#Hyphal presence lm plot - remove outlier for waste
SOM_13C_T0 %>%
  filter(g_debris < 750) %>%
ggplot(aes(x=g_debris, y=AM_hyph_per)) + 
	geom_point(aes(color=Site_ID), size=2) +
  scale_color_manual(values=colors4) + #define colors to use
  geom_smooth(method="lm", se=TRUE, color=plotline_color, fill=fill_color) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1)) + #change to %
  xlab("Colliery Waste (g/mesocosm)") + ylab("Presence of AM Hyphae (% of Root)") + #define/change X and Y labels
  my_theme

ggsave('AM_hyph_waste1.svg', #save plot name and type - can be "eps", "pdf", "jpeg", "tiff", "png", "bmp", "svg"
       path = "Figures", #save to folder
       width = 6, height = 4, units = "in", #set dimensions
       dpi = 300, #set resolution
       bg=NULL) #background from plot specifications

shapiro.test(resid(lm(AM_hyph_per ~ g_debris + Site_ID, data = SOM_13C_T0))) #check normality of residuals - normal
summary(aov(AM_hyph_per ~ g_debris + Site_ID, data = SOM_13C_T0)) #debris sig, site almost

Anova(lmer(AM_hyph_per ~ g_debris + (1|Site_ID), 
    REML = TRUE, #restricted maximum likelihood (REML) for model comparison 
    data = SOM_13C_T0, #choose dataframe
    na.action = na.omit), type=3) #debris very

AM_debris_lme <- lmer(AM_hyph_per ~ g_debris + (1|Site_ID), 
    REML = TRUE, #restricted maximum likelihood (REML) for model comparison 
    data = SOM_13C_T0, #choose dataframe
    na.action = na.omit)
summary(AM_debris_lme) #random accounts for less variance
shapiro.test(resid(AM_debris_lme)) #normal
performance::r2(AM_debris_lme) #calculate R-squared for model fit
MuMIn::AICc(AM_debris_lme, k=2) #calculate AICc for for model comparison with small sample sizes
```

## Beta diversity
Diversity between sites

### 16S
```{r 16S beta}



```

### ITS 

#### ASVs

```{r ITS rarefaction curve asv, warning=FALSE}

#ASV counts per site - rarefaction
its_rare.out <- rarecurve(asv_ITS, step = 10, tidy = TRUE)
its_rare.out$Site <- as.factor(its_rare.out$Site)
its_rare.out$sample.label <- as.factor(its_rare.out$Sample)
its_rare.out$label <- NA

for (i in unique(its_rare.out$Site)) {
  tmp <- its_rare.out[which(its_rare.out$Site==i),]
  its_rare.out$label[which(its_rare.out$Sample==max(tmp$Sample)&its_rare.out$Site==i)] <- i
}

#plot rarefaction curve
ggplot(data = its_rare.out, aes(x = Sample, y = Species, group = Site)) +
  geom_line(color = "black", linewidth = 1) +
  #geom_point() +
  labs(x = "Number of reads", y = "ASVs", title = "Rarefaction curve") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1),legend.position = 0) +
  scale_color_discrete(name = "Site") +
  geom_label_repel(aes(label = label),
                   nudge_x = 1,
                   na.rm = TRUE) + 
  my_theme

ggsave('ITS_rarecurve.svg', #save plot name and type - can be "eps", "pdf", "jpeg", "tiff", "png", "bmp", "svg"
       path = "Figures", #save to folder
       width = 6, height = 4, units = "in", #set dimensions
       dpi = 300, #set resolution
       bg=NULL) #background from plot specifications

```

```{r ITS beta asv, warning=FALSE}

#calculate distances

#Euclidean distance
its_euc.list <-  replicate(100, matrix(nrow = dim(asv_ITS)[1], ncol = dim(asv_ITS)[1]), simplify = FALSE)
for (i in 1:100) {
  its_euc.list[[i]] <- vegdist(sqrt(as.matrix(rrarefy(asv_ITS,sample=170))/170), method="euc")
}
asv_ITS.ml.euc <- Reduce("+", its_euc.list) / length(its_euc.list)

#Jaqcard distance
its_jaq.list <-  replicate(100, matrix(nrow = dim(asv_ITS)[1], ncol = dim(asv_ITS)[1]), simplify = FALSE)
for (i in 1:100) {
  its_jaq.list[[i]] <- vegdist(as.matrix(rrarefy(asv_ITS,sample=170)), method="jaccard", binary = TRUE)
}
asv_ITS.jaq <- Reduce("+", its_jaq.list) / length(its_jaq.list)

#Bray-Curtis
its_bray.list <-  replicate(100, matrix(nrow = dim(asv_ITS)[1], ncol = dim(asv_ITS)[1]), simplify = FALSE)
for (i in 1:100) {
  its_bray.list[[i]] <- vegdist(as.matrix(rrarefy(asv_ITS,sample=170))/170, method="bray")
}
asv_ITS.ml.bray <- Reduce("+", its_bray.list) / length(its_bray.list)


#check beta dispersion by site for each distance metric
mod <- betadisper(asv_ITS.ml.euc, env_ITS$Site_ID, type = "centroid")
permutest(mod, permutations = 999) #P=0.002

mod <- betadisper(asv_ITS.jaq, env_ITS$Site_ID, type = "centroid")
permutest(mod, permutations = 999) #P=0.001

mod <- betadisper(asv_ITS.ml.bray, env_ITS$Site_ID, type = "centroid")
permutest(mod, permutations = 999) #P=0.001

#PERMANOVA
adonis2(asv_ITS.ml.euc ~ Site_ID, method = "none", data = env_ITS, permutations = 9999) #P=1e-4
adonis2(asv_ITS.jaq ~ Site_ID, method = "none", data = env_ITS, permutations = 9999) #P=1e-4
adonis2(asv_ITS.ml.bray ~ Site_ID, method = "none", data = env_ITS, permutations = 9999) #P=1e-4


#check beta dispersion by pH for each distance metric
mod <- betadisper(asv_ITS.ml.euc, env_ITS$pH, type = "centroid")
permutest(mod, permutations = 999) #P=0.001

mod <- betadisper(asv_ITS.jaq, env_ITS$pH, type = "centroid")
permutest(mod, permutations = 999) #P=0.001

mod <- betadisper(asv_ITS.ml.bray, env_ITS$pH, type = "centroid")
permutest(mod, permutations = 999) #P=0.001

#PERMANOVA
adonis2(asv_ITS.ml.euc ~ pH, method = "none", data = env_ITS, permutations = 9999) #P=1e-4
adonis2(asv_ITS.jaq ~ pH, method = "none", data = env_ITS, permutations = 9999) #P=1e-4
adonis2(asv_ITS.ml.bray ~ pH, method = "none", data = env_ITS, permutations = 9999) #P=1e-4


#check beta dispersion - plant richness
```

##### NMDS

```{r ITS NMDS asv, warning=FALSE}

#Hellinger (square root) transform and standardize with vegan library
asv_ITS_h_std <- asv_ITS %>%
  dplyr::select((where(is.numeric))) %>% #select only numeric columns
  decostand(., #call decostand transformation function
				 method = "hellinger", #transformation method
				 zap = FALSE, #make near zero values into zeros to avoid exaggeration
				 na.rm = TRUE) %>% #remove NA values
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~scale(., center = TRUE, scale = TRUE)))

#standardize env variables
env_ITS_std <- env_ITS[,-c(17:30)] %>% #env file minus microbial diversity and incomplete columns
  mutate_if(is.numeric,scale) 

its_nmds_df <- asv_ITS_h_std

#test how many axes are appropriate
stress <- vector(length = 6)
for (i in 1:6) {
    stress[i] <- metaMDS(its_nmds_df, distance = "bray", k = i,
                         model = "global", #calc stress on ranks of data
                         maxit = 400, #max iterations of configuration adjustments
                         try = 20, trymax = 20, #min and max runs
                         autotransform = FALSE, #don't transform data
                         weakties = TRUE, #set fitted distances as un-fixed
                         scaling = TRUE, #re-scale ordination axes
                         na.rm = TRUE)$stress
}
names(stress) <- paste0(1:6, "Dim")
par(mar = c(3.5,3.5,1,1), mgp = c(2, 0.6, 0), cex = 0.8, las = 2)
barplot(stress, ylab = "stress")

#run NMDS with 5 axes to be reliably stress < 0.2
set.seed(42) #set seed for reproducibility
its_nmds <- metaMDS(its_nmds_df, 
                distance = "bray", #data & distance measure
                k = 3, #number of axes
                model = "global", #calc stress on ranks of data
                maxit = 400, #max iterations of configuration adjustments
                try = 20, trymax = 200, #min and max runs
                autotransform = FALSE, #don't transform data
                weakties = TRUE, #set fitted distances as un-fixed
                pc = TRUE, #rotate axes using PCA to orient first 2 axes as containing most of the variability
                scaling = TRUE, #re-scale ordination axes to ‘unit root mean squares’
                na.rm = TRUE) #remove NA values

its_nmds #check "stress" value to see how well the data is represented by the ordination
goodness(its_nmds) #check goodness of fit for each point
stressplot(its_nmds, main = "Shepard plot") #diagnostic plot

#make fit vectors with env variables and view
#its_nmdsfit <- envfit(its_nmds, env_ITS[,-c(1:4,17:30)], #without standardization
 #                     permutations = 999, na.rm=TRUE)
its_nmdsfit <- envfit(its_nmds, env_ITS_std[,-c(1:4)], #with standardization
                      permutations = 999, na.rm=TRUE)
its_nmdsfit #check fit vectors

#make df of scores, add sites
its_nmds_scores <- as.data.frame(scores(its_nmds))
its_nmds_scores$Site_ID = env_ITS$Site_ID 

#make df of vectors, only significant vectors
its_nmds_vectors <- as.data.frame(scores(its_nmdsfit, display = "vectors")) #extracts relevant scores from envfit
its_nmds_vectors <- cbind(its_nmds_vectors, variable = rownames(its_nmds_vectors)) #and then gives them their names
its_nmds_vectors <- cbind(its_nmds_vectors, pval = its_nmdsfit$vectors$pvals) # add pvalues to dataframe
its_sig_vectors <- subset(its_nmds_vectors, pval<=0.1) #subset data to show variables somewhat significant at rounded 0.1

#plot scores with ggplot
ggplot(its_nmds_scores) + 
  geom_point(size = 2, aes(x = NMDS1, y = NMDS2, color = Site_ID)) +
  stat_ellipse(aes(x = NMDS1, y = NMDS2, color = Site_ID, fill = Site_ID),
               alpha = 0.2, #transparency of ellipse fill
               geom = "polygon") + #draw as polygon rather than just outline
  geom_segment(data = its_sig_vectors,
              aes(x = 0, xend = NMDS1 * 400,
                  y = 0, yend = NMDS2 * 400), 
              arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.25,"cm"),
                            type = "open", angle = 20,
                            ends = "last"),
              color = "grey10", 
              lwd = 0.3) +
  geom_text_repel(data = its_sig_vectors,
                  aes(x = NMDS1 * 400,
                      y = NMDS2 * 400, 
                      label = variable), 
                  size = 3,
                  max.overlaps = Inf) +
  scale_color_manual(values = colors4) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = colors4) + #match fill colors to your color scheme
  labs(x = "NMDS1", y = "NMDS2", color = "Site", fill = "Site") +
  coord_fixed() +
  my_theme

#save figure - name, type, folder, dimensions, resolution, background specs
ggsave('ITS_asv_NMDS_210526.svg', path = "Figures", width = 6, height = 4, units = "in", dpi = 300, bg=NULL)

```

##### NMDS

```{r ITS NMDS g, warning=FALSE}

#Hellinger (square root) transform and standardize with vegan library
asv_ITS_g_h_std <- asv_ITS.g %>%
  dplyr::select((where(is.numeric))) %>% #select only numeric columns
  decostand(., #call decostand transformation function
				 method = "hellinger", #transformation method
				 zap = FALSE, #make near zero values into zeros to avoid exaggeration
				 na.rm = TRUE) %>% #remove NA values
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~scale(., center = TRUE, scale = TRUE)))

its_nmds_df <- asv_ITS_g_h_std

#test how many axes are appropriate
stress <- vector(length = 6)
for (i in 1:6) {
    stress[i] <- metaMDS(its_nmds_df, distance = "bray", k = i,
                         model = "global", #calc stress on ranks of data
                         maxit = 400, #max iterations of configuration adjustments
                         try = 20, trymax = 20, #min and max runs
                         autotransform = FALSE, #don't transform data
                         weakties = TRUE, #set fitted distances as un-fixed
                         scaling = TRUE, #re-scale ordination axes
                         na.rm = TRUE)$stress
}
names(stress) <- paste0(1:6, "Dim")
par(mar = c(3.5,3.5,1,1), mgp = c(2, 0.6, 0), cex = 0.8, las = 2)
barplot(stress, ylab = "stress")

#run NMDS with 5 axes to be reliably stress < 0.2
set.seed(42) #set seed for reproducibility
its_nmds <- metaMDS(its_nmds_df, 
                distance = "bray", #data & distance measure
                k = 3, #number of axes
                model = "global", #calc stress on ranks of data
                maxit = 400, #max iterations of configuration adjustments
                try = 20, trymax = 200, #min and max runs
                autotransform = FALSE, #don't transform data
                weakties = TRUE, #set fitted distances as un-fixed
                pc = TRUE, #rotate axes using PCA to orient first 2 axes as containing most of the variability
                scaling = TRUE, #re-scale ordination axes to ‘unit root mean squares’
                na.rm = TRUE) #remove NA values

its_nmds #check "stress" value to see how well the data is represented by the ordination
goodness(its_nmds) #check goodness of fit for each point
stressplot(its_nmds, main = "Shepard plot") #diagnostic plot

#make fit vectors with env variables and view
#its_nmdsfit <- envfit(its_nmds, env_ITS[,-c(1:4,17:30)], #without standardization
 #                     permutations = 999, na.rm=TRUE)
its_nmdsfit <- envfit(its_nmds, env_ITS_std[,-c(1:4)], #with standardization
                      permutations = 999, na.rm=TRUE)
its_nmdsfit #check fit vectors

#make df of scores, add sites
its_nmds_scores <- as.data.frame(scores(its_nmds))
its_nmds_scores$Site_ID = env_ITS$Site_ID 

#make df of vectors, only significant vectors
its_nmds_vectors <- as.data.frame(scores(its_nmdsfit, display = "vectors")) #extracts relevant scores from envfit
its_nmds_vectors <- cbind(its_nmds_vectors, variable = rownames(its_nmds_vectors)) #and then gives them their names
its_nmds_vectors <- cbind(its_nmds_vectors, pval = its_nmdsfit$vectors$pvals) # add pvalues to dataframe
its_sig_vectors <- subset(its_nmds_vectors, pval<=0.1) #subset data to show variables somewhat significant at rounded 0.1

#plot scores with ggplot
ggplot(its_nmds_scores) + 
  geom_point(size = 2, aes(x = NMDS1, y = NMDS2, color = Site_ID)) +
  stat_ellipse(aes(x = NMDS1, y = NMDS2, color = Site_ID, fill = Site_ID),
               alpha = 0.2, #transparency of ellipse fill
               geom = "polygon") + #draw as polygon rather than just outline
  geom_segment(data = its_sig_vectors,
              aes(x = 0, xend = NMDS1 * 400,
                  y = 0, yend = NMDS2 * 400), 
              arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.25,"cm"),
                            type = "open", angle = 20,
                            ends = "last"),
              color = "grey10", 
              lwd = 0.3) +
  geom_text_repel(data = its_sig_vectors,
                  aes(x = NMDS1 * 400,
                      y = NMDS2 * 400, 
                      label = variable), 
                  size = 3,
                  max.overlaps = Inf) +
  scale_color_manual(values = colors4) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = colors4) + #match fill colors to your color scheme
  labs(x = "NMDS1", y = "NMDS2", color = "Site", fill = "Site") +
  coord_fixed() +
  my_theme

#save figure - name, type, folder, dimensions, resolution, background specs
ggsave('ITS_g_NMDS_210526.svg', path = "Figures", width = 6, height = 4, units = "in", dpi = 300, bg=NULL)

```
